walkthroughs.body_html:
Wildlife adapts in clever ways:

• Polar bear — thick fur, blubber, large feet
• Arctic fox — white winter coat
• Caribou — migrate to find food
• Marram-like low-growing plants reduce wind exposure

Cold regions hold valuable resources:

• Oil & gas (Alaska, Siberia)
• Minerals (gold, diamonds)
• Fishing (Bering Sea)
• Tourism (cruises, Northern Lights)

But development risks huge ecological damage.

Cold regions warm 2-4x faster than global average!

• Melting sea ice threatens polar bears
• Thawing permafrost releases methane
• Lower albedo = more warming
• Indigenous livelihoods threatened

A dangerous feedback loop.

mcqs.q: What is the difference between primary and secondary effects of an earthquake?
options: Primary effects happen first and secondary effects happen the next day.
Primary effects are the worst effects and secondary effects are minor.
Tundra is in the Arctic and taiga is in the Antarctic.
Primary effects occur immediately as a direct result of shaking (building collapse, deaths); secondary effects follow afterwards (fires, tsunamis, disease, homelessness).

mcqs.q: Why does deforestation increase flood risk?
options: Deforestation has no effect on rivers — only rainfall matters.
Primary effects happen first and secondary effects happen the next day.
Deforestation causes floods because trees normally hold water in their branches forever.
Trees intercept rainfall, their roots increase infiltration and transpiration removes water — removing them increases surface runoff and reduces lag time, peaking river levels faster.

mcqs.q: What is the difference between the tundra and the taiga biomes?
options: Tundra is treeless cold biome (too cold and permafrost-dominated for trees), while taiga (boreal forest) is the band of coniferous forest just south of the tundra in subarctic latitudes.
Tundra and taiga are the same biome with different names.
Tundra is in the Arctic and taiga is in the Antarctic.
Deforestation has no effect on rivers — only rainfall matters.
